sources.title: Dizionario leccese-italiano (online edition)
sources.author: Antonio Garrisi
sources.license: All rights reserved (author's work published online)
sources.reliability_notes: Large single-author dictionary of the Lecce/Cavallino variety with full verb paradigms, usage examples, about 1,200 proverbs and an explicit orthographic note on the cacuminal sound (written δδ) and the simple/long sh sounds (sç/sc). It is not peer-reviewed, but it is the most detailed open source for the city variety and agrees with the academic descriptions. The front matter was read in full. All letter pages (A-Z) were downloaded and searched entry by entry for the items used. Definitions were rewritten in our own words, not copied.
sources.relevant_sections: Prefazione/Avvertenze (pronunciation and raddoppiamento rules); entries for verbs (aìre, èssere, fare, dire, ulìre, putìre, sapìre, sçire, stare, enìre, tare, ìtere, tenìre); function words; interjections; proverbs and 'modi di dire'; vulgar entries (cazzu, mìnchia, fessa, culu, curnutu, futtìre, mannàggia, etc.)

sources.title: Dialetti salentini
sources.linguistic_area: Salento (provinces of Lecce, Brindisi, south-eastern Taranto)
sources.reliability_notes: Encyclopedic summary drawing on Rohlfs, Mancarella, Parlangeli, Morosi, Panareo and Ribezzo. Used for the three-way north/centre/south division, vowel systems, syntax ('ku'/'ka', the future and progressive periphrases, the imperfect-indicative hypothetical), the pronoun table, 'signurìa', and the proverbs and phrases it lists. Facts were rephrased.
sources.relevant_sections: Fonetica, Sintassi, Morfologia, Varianti, Dialetti salentini e dialetti pugliesi, Proverbi, Fraseologia

sources.title: Dialetto leccese
sources.reliability_notes: Used for the Lecce present/imperfect/perfect of essere, avere and scire, the progressive 'sta + finite verb', the future strategies, local differences (bu vs ve, li vs le, the Grecìa remote past, 'sta me uardi' vs 'me sta uardi') and a long list of common words.
sources.relevant_sections: Differenze dall'italiano standard, Altre differenze territoriali, Verbi, Parole di uso comune

sources.title: Dialetto salentino meridionale
sources.linguistic_area: Southern Salento (south of the Gallipoli-Maglie-Otranto line)
sources.reliability_notes: Used only for the contrasts with the southern variety: no conditioned diphthongs, affricated cacuminal (beddhru), unstressed vowels tending to a.

sources.title: Salentino dialect
sources.reliability_notes: Classification (Extreme Southern Italian, after Avolio 2012). It also gives a small sample of sentences, taken from Golovko & Panov (aggiu ffare, iddu ulia cu llu ddicu, ci tinia fame mangiava). The page carries 'more citations needed' tags.

sources.title: Siciliani, calabresi e salentini, dialetti (Enciclopedia dell'Italiano)
sources.author: Francesco Avolio
sources.reliability_notes: Scholarly encyclopedia article. Used for the five-vowel stressed system, the cacuminal outcome of -ll-, cacuminal tr/str, the wɛ diphthong (bbuenu vs bbona), voiceless stops kept after nasals, the 'ku' clause replacing the infinitive, the repeated imperfect in counterfactuals, crai 'tomorrow', and the spellings dd/ddh/ddr.

sources.title: Vocabolario dei dialetti salentini (Terra d'Otranto), vol. III: Supplemento, Repertorio italiano-salentino, Indici
sources.author: Gerhard Rohlfs
sources.publisher: Bayerische Akademie der Wissenschaften (open PDF on tll-open.badw.de)
sources.license: Copyright 1961 Bayerische Akademie der Wissenschaften; made openly available online by the Academy
sources.reliability_notes: The standard reference work. Only volume III (the Italian-Salentino repertory) was available and was read through text extraction. Volumes I-II (the Salentine-Italian part, with locality labels) were not consulted, so Rohlfs is cited only for facts checked in vol. III: the forms listed under 'bestemmia', 'stupido', 'pene', 'nessuno', 'lavorare' and 'andare'. Its entries are pan-Salentine and often lack a locality, so Lecce forms were always confirmed in Garrisi.

sources.title: I dialetti perileccesi
sources.author: Antonio Romano
sources.publisher: In P. Pascali & D. Capone (eds.), L'ombra di Tancredi, Giorgiani (author's manuscript on AperTO, Università di Torino)
sources.linguistic_area: Dialects around Lecce (Cavallino, Lizzanello, Lequile, Monteroni, Vernole, Trepuzzi, Squinzano)
sources.license: Open access author's manuscript (rights with author/publisher)
sources.reliability_notes: Peer-level academic description. It lists the features shared around Lecce: cacuminal -ḍḍ-, Sicilian-type vowels with metaphonic diphthongs ie/ue, the 2pl clitic bbu, the 'Lecce-type' possessives, reduced use of the infinitive, the progressive order 'se sta' (rather than 'sta sse') and regular raddoppiamento fonosintattico. It also gives the full possessive set (miu/mia/mei; tou/toa/toi; sou/soa/soi; nuesciu/noscia/nuesci/nosce; uesciu/oscia/uesci/osce; loru).

sources.title: Proverbi salentini
sources.reliability_notes: A short list of sourced proverbs (citing Romano, Malecore, Lezzi and local press). Spellings vary by locality, so only items consistent with Lecce forms were used.
